Subject: Order Form insurance: endorsement language, COI timing, and broker coordination

Hi Maya —

Thanks for moving the order form along. Legal is reviewing the redlines and has a few specific asks on insurance so we can close procurement this week. Can you confirm the insurer will provide the following?:

- General liability: $1,000,000 per occurrence; $2,000,000 aggregate (or umbrella $5M).
- Professional / E&O: $1,000,000 per claim (where applicable for services).
- Cyber/privacy: $1,000,000 each event (Beacon stores/processes customer data).
- Workers comp statutory limits.

Also we need:
- A certificate of insurance (COI) naming "Redwood Inference, Inc." as additional insured via endorsement (not just a certificate note).
- Additional insured endorsement wording: primary and non-contributory and waiver of subrogation.
- If the carrier cannot add all elements, please provide the carrier contact and an ETA for the endorsement.

Can you attach a preview COI and a draft endorsement text (carrier-ready) so our Legal team can confirm? Procurement prefers COI+endorsement before countersignature; if you can get the broker to send a draft endorsement today, we can sign the order form pending final carrier confirmation.

We are on a tight timeline — ideally signatures this week. Who on the carrier/broker side should I loop in?

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Hi all — Tim from BrokeragePlus here. Thanks for the note — confirmed we can issue a COI immediately and prepare the endorsement. A few practical notes from the carrier side:

- COI: we'll upload a standard COI showing coverage limits; that is not a substitute for an additional insured endorsement.
- Endorsement: most carriers will provide an AI endorsement that names the additional insured and notes primary/non-contributory; however, waiver of subrogation is carrier-dependent and sometimes requires an endorsement to the policy wording.
- Wording: carriers sometimes insist on limited-form AI endorsements rather than broad blanket language. We can request the broader language but it may require underwriter sign-off (typically 48–72 hours).
- Retroactive date (for E&O/professional liability) — if Redwood needs a retroactive date, please confirm; otherwise we will use policy inception.

Proposed next steps:
1) Redwood confirms exact named insured wording for the endorsement (e.g., \"Redwood Inference, Inc. and its affiliates\" vs \"Redwood Inference, Inc., Attn: Contracts\").
2) We request the carrier produce a carrier-backed endorsement draft and an estimated time to bind (I expect 2–4 business days).
3) If an immediate execution is required, we can provide a COI + broker letter as interim evidence and commit to endorsement within the ETA.

Lauren — tagging you to confirm whether procurement/legal is OK with the interim COI+broker-letter approach or if you need the full endorsement before countersignature.

Best,
Tim Brooks
Senior Risk Advisor
BrokeragePlus

Attachment: Beacon_Proof_of_Insurance_2026.pdf
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Tim Brooks <t.brooks@brokerageplus.com>, Maya Kline <maya.k@beaconcloud.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form insurance: endorsement language, COI timing, and broker coordination

Thanks Tim — this is helpful. Procurement/legal are willing to accept the interim COI + broker letter to start the commercial relationship BUT we need a firm commitment on the endorsement delivery timeline before we countersign. A few specifics we require:

- Endorsement must name: "Redwood Inference, Inc." and also list "Redwood Services, LLC" as a named additional insured on the endorsement form.
- The endorsement should include primary and non-contributory language; waiver of subrogation should be included if the carrier can provide it. If the carrier refuses, we need written confirmation and the carrier contact.
- For E&O retroactive date: not required unless Beacon requests retro coverage; keep policy inception as default.
- Interim evidence: acceptable only if the broker sends a one-page commitment letter with a clear ETA (date) for endorsement delivery.

Hannah — can you please confirm the cyber limit $1M is sufficient for Security? If not, let us know the required number by EOD tomorrow so we can re-request from carrier.

Maya/Tim — once you have carrier confirmation, please send the carrier-backed endorsement draft and COI to contracts@redwood.com. We'll hold countersignature until endorsement delivery or the broker letter commitment is received with the ETA.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference
